breaking.headline: Dow closes higher after erasing a 1,105-point plunge
breaking.fact: The Dow finished up 164.25 points (+0.33%) at 50,182.95 after losing 1,105 at the morning low; the S&P 500 cut a 3.2% plunge to -0.25% and the Nasdaq trimmed a 4.6% drop to -0.62% as bargain hunters stepped in. Markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving.

breaking.headline: S&P puts Nvidia's AA rating on CreditWatch Negative
breaking.fact: S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia's AA credit rating on CreditWatch Negative, citing rising management and governance risks after Jensen Huang's departure and reinstatement; a downgrade within 90 days would likely be limited to one notch, to AA-.

breaking.headline: U.S. finds no evidence China directed spying on Nvidia CEO, WSJ reports
breaking.fact: U.S. officials found no evidence that China directed an executive to spy on Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, the Wall Street Journal reported, undercutting one thread of the probes around his exit and return.

breaking.headline: Gold stages a $160 rebound off a 14-month low
breaking.fact: Spot gold fell below $3,450 in the morning, then rebounded to close near $3,588, up about 0.9% on the day, while silver recovered above $41 as Treasury yields fell and stocks bounced.

watchlist.name: Air Liquide
watchlist.blurb: Air Liquide closed in Paris at €188.46, worth $206.08 at the ECB's Nov 25 rate of 1.0935, up 0.2% on a day U.S. stocks plunged then mostly recovered. The industrial-gas giant's defensive profile did its quiet work again as tech cratered, and the dollar price held near the top of its range with the euro above 1.09. No company news today; watch whether the euro holds 1.09 into Friday's short session.

watchlist.name: Anthropic
watchlist.blurb: Anthropic closed at $82.79, up 1.1% on the day but back below its $83 IPO price after touching $84.57 in the afternoon rally. The stock is down from its debut and has now closed below the $83 IPO price two days running as investors keep questioning debt-fueled AI spending. Sean's IPO allocation is narrowly underwater again; watch whether $83 flips back to support in Friday's holiday-shortened session.

watchlist.name: SPDR Bloomberg 1-3 Mo T-Bill
watchlist.blurb: BIL edged up to $91.64, a quiet 0.03% gain on a wild day that saw the Nasdaq plunge 4.6% before recovering most of it. The Treasury-bill ETF keeps doing its job as the portfolio's cash anchor, paying a 4.04% distribution yield while stocks whipsaw around it. With the Fed now nearly certain to hike in December, short-term yields stay supported; BIL remains the calmest line on the tape.

watchlist.name: Alphabet
watchlist.blurb: Alphabet fell 2.1% to $273.10, giving back more ground as the AI selloff rolled on and the cost of insuring its debt against default hit a record, per S&P Global data. The stock is down about 14% over the past month as investors punish the debt-fueled AI buildout and brace for a Fed hike. The cloud and search businesses keep growing underneath the noise; watch Friday's short session for buyers near $270.

watchlist.name: Eli Lilly
watchlist.blurb: Eli Lilly slipped 1.1% to $1,392.22, caught in the broad selloff even as defensive healthcare names held up better than tech. The drugmaker's weight-loss and diabetes franchises remain the growth engine, and the shares have held the $1,350–$1,400 range through the recent chop. No company news today; watch whether the shares stabilize above $1,380 if the market finds its footing after Thanksgiving.

watchlist.name: Cheniere Energy
watchlist.blurb: Cheniere rose 2.0% to $301.99, one of the day's winners as natural-gas-linked names rallied and WTI crude jumped 2.6% to $84.15. LNG exporters keep benefiting from strong global gas demand and the Hormuz standoff, which has traders pricing supply risk into every energy barrel. The stock has held near $300 through the recent chop; watch whether it holds above $300 into the holiday-shortened week.

watchlist.name: Nvidia
watchlist.blurb: Nvidia fell 3.9% to $149.30, its second straight loss, after an early plunge of nearly 9% as the AI rout deepened. S&P Global put its AA credit rating on CreditWatch Negative, citing governance risks around Huang's exit and reinstatement, with any downgrade likely limited to one notch. U.S. officials found no evidence China directed spying on Huang, per the WSJ. Sean's holding stays a long-term hold.

watchlist.name: Pfizer
watchlist.blurb: Pfizer was flat at $28.46 on a day the market plunged then roared back, the drugmaker's dividend and defensive profile keeping it out of the fray. The stock has traded between $27.40 and $28.47 over the past week, a narrow band that says the market can't decide what to do with it. No company news today; the dividend remains the story while the shares wait for a catalyst into year-end.

watchlist.name: Rocket Lab
watchlist.blurb: Rocket Lab rose 2.3% to $47.02, recovering with the afternoon rally after the morning's broad selloff. The space stock keeps drawing interest as launch cadence grows and investors look past the day-to-day swings in the AI trade. No company news today; the shares have held the mid-$40s through the recent chop, and Friday's short session will test whether the bounce has legs.

watchlist.name: Rithm Capital
watchlist.blurb: Rithm Capital gained 2.9% to $8.92, one of the tape's better performers as the market clawed back from its morning lows. The mortgage REIT's dividend keeps drawing income buyers even with a December hike now nearly certain after the hot PCE print. The shares have climbed from $8.05 a week ago as the 10-year yield slipped to 4.85%; watch whether they can hold above $8.90 into December.

watchlist.name: SpaceX
watchlist.blurb: SPCX rose 1.3% to $127.44, tracking the afternoon recovery as risk appetite returned after the morning rout. The SPAC-focused fund tends to move with small-cap sentiment, which outperformed today with the Russell 2000 up 0.7%. No fund-specific news; the shares have slipped from the low-$140s over the past week as SPAC sentiment cooled, and Friday's short session will show whether the bounce holds.

watchlist.name: Truist Financial
watchlist.blurb: Truist rose 0.9% to $47.89, a quiet gain as bank shares steadied while the Dow erased a 1,105-point plunge to close higher. Regional banks have been range-bound as the Fed's hiking path firms up, with December now nearly certain after the hot PCE print. No company news today; the dividend and the bank's Southeastern footprint remain the anchors while rates stay high and the Fed keeps hiking.

watchlist.name: U.S. Antimony
watchlist.blurb: U.S. Antimony rose 1.4% to $2.21, holding near its recent highs as the critical-minerals trade stays in focus. The stock fired the bottom-watch signal at Monday's $2.39 close and has since eased back toward $2.20. Antimony's role in defense supply chains keeps it on the watchlist; watch whether $2.20 holds as support if the market turns choppy again after the holiday.

watchlist.name: Uranium Energy
watchlist.blurb: Uranium Energy rose 2.2% to $5.69, bouncing with the afternoon recovery after Monday's bottom-watch fire at $5.84. The uranium miner remains well off its autumn highs as the sector consolidates, but the long-term nuclear-buildout thesis is intact and the stock keeps finding buyers near $5.50. Watch whether it can reclaim $5.84, the level that tripped the bottom signal, in Friday's short session.

watchlist.name: VI5TC (est.)
watchlist.blurb: The S&P-anchored estimate for VI5TC slipped to $147.64 as the index gave back 0.25% to close at 7,182.78, cutting a 3.2% morning plunge to a modest loss. The estimate tracks the S&P 500's close off the Nov 3 anchor of $155.58 at 7,568.92, so it moves tick-for-tick with the index. With markets closed Thursday, the next read comes after the holiday; the estimate stands until Dave's account value updates it.

watchlist.name: Valero Energy
watchlist.blurb: Valero slipped 0.5% to $323.00 as crude's rally failed to lift refiners on a day the Dow erased a 1,105-point drop. WTI jumped 2.6% to $84.15 on the Hormuz standoff, but refining margins are the swing factor here, not the crude price itself. The shares have eased from the mid-$360s over the past week; watch whether the stock holds $320 if crude keeps climbing into the holiday.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Target 2035
watchlist.blurb: Vanguard's Target Retirement 2035 fund held at a $28.43 NAV, its latest posted value, drifting 0.3% lower as stocks slipped on the day. The balanced fund's mix of U.S. and international stocks and bonds keeps it steadier than the tape, which plunged then recovered most of its losses. The next NAV posts after tonight's close; the fund's glide path keeps trimming stock exposure as 2035 approaches.

watchlist.name: Schwab Value Advantage MF
watchlist.blurb: Schwab's money fund holds at $1.00 with a 7-day yield of 3.78%, published Nov 24, unchanged from the last print. The sweep vehicle keeps earning while stocks swing, and per Sean's plan any balance over $1,000 in an account gets sold for a CD. The position should keep evaporating over time; watch the December Fed hike, which would nudge the yield higher, and the next print in the morning.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Treasury MMF
watchlist.blurb: Vanguard's Treasury money fund holds at $1.00 with a 7-day SEC yield of 4.04%, published Nov 24, unchanged from the last print. It remains the top-yielding cash parking spot, beating SWVXX by 26 basis points, and the home for Sean's Treasury cash at eTrade. The yield tracks the Fed's path closely and the fund owns only Treasuries, so there is no credit risk; watch the December hike for the next move.

weekInBrief.headline: Durable goods orders rise just 0.2% in October
weekInBrief.body: New orders for U.S. durable goods rose 0.2% in October to $346.7 billion, below the 0.5% economists expected, after a 2.0% September jump. Excluding transportation, orders rose 0.5%, and core capital goods orders — a proxy for business investment — rose 0.6%, keeping the investment picture intact.

weekInBrief.headline: Deere misses on earnings but jumps 4.4% as management calls the ag bottom
weekInBrief.body: Deere earned $3.89 a share in its fiscal fourth quarter, below the $4.07 consensus, as large-agriculture sales fell 15% and operating profit there dropped 33%. But shares rose 4.4% to $641.02 as management said the farm-equipment cycle bottomed in 2026 and guided fiscal 2027 net income of $4.50–$5.25 billion.

weekInBrief.headline: New tariffs could push inflation back up in 2027
weekInBrief.body: The administration's proposed tariffs on 14 economies risk driving consumer prices up again next year, just as the price rises from earlier tariffs were starting to fade. Core PCE inflation already ran at 3.3% in October, well above the Fed's 2% target, and the new duties would land on top of it.

weekInBrief.headline: Hot core PCE puts a January rate hike on the table
weekInBrief.body: October's 3.3% core PCE reading — the highest since November 2023 — leaves a December quarter-point hike nearly certain at 94% odds, with traders now pricing a 51.5% chance of a second hike by January 27 and a further increase certain by March.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: A third tanker struck a mine and caught fire in the Strait later on Wednesday, Iran's Fars agency said, hours after the IRGC Navy claimed two tankers hit mines in the morning; the claims remain unverified and the vessels unnamed. The U.S. Virtual Embassy in Iran told American citizens to leave the country at once. Tehran offered through Qatari mediators to reopen the strait within 48 hours if Washington lifts the naval blockade and ends the war on all fronts, while its parliament speaker's seven conditions for talks remain on the table. CENTCOM says its blockade has kept Iran from loading any crude oil since late August, and Kpler still puts Iranian oil on the water outside the blockade zone at zero, with the 40 to 50 million barrels already in Asia discharging in China at close to 1 million barrels a day, while non-Iranian Gulf oil keeps flowing at roughly 70% of pre-war volumes.

space.headline: ISS crew runs biomedical research ahead of Thanksgiving cargo delivery
space.body: Expedition 75 worked biomedical research aboard the station Wednesday, with ultrasound scans and blood-pressure checks, as the crew prepared for the Progress 97 cargo ship's arrival on Thanksgiving Day carrying about three tons of food, fuel and supplies. Northrop Grumman's Cygnus XL is set to launch Sunday, Nov. 29, with research on cancer cell movement and engineered muscle tissue.

space.headline: Space radiation leaves a hidden, sex-specific mark on the brain
space.body: A NASA-funded study in mice found simulated galactic cosmic radiation triggered distinct molecular responses in the brain's immune cells — male microglia shifted stress adaptation and metabolism, female microglia showed broader drops in immune signaling — with no immediate cognitive problems. The work, published Nov. 20 in Scientific Reports, raises questions about long missions to the Moon and Mars.

space.headline: Lunar craters could shield moon-base nuclear reactors for free
space.body: Simulations from Los Alamos, NASA Glenn, Oak Ridge, Idaho National Lab and Lockheed Martin show placing a 40 kW fission reactor behind a 120-metre crater wall near Shackleton Crater cuts radiation at a nearby habitat to near zero — about four-hundredths of a rem a year — letting the reactor's own shield protect only nearby electronics.

space.headline: A hidden planet twice Earth's mass may lurk beyond Neptune
space.body: Simulations spanning 4.5 billion years, published Nov. 23 in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, show a hypothetical planet about twice Earth's mass orbiting 350–500 AU out could explain the strange tilted and detached orbits of icy bodies beyond Neptune. It is distinct from the Planet Nine idea, and the Vera Rubin Observatory's survey can test the prediction.

apod.title: Tossing Fireworks from Cloud to Cloud
apod.explanation: Astronauts aboard the International Space Station see lightning from above, where bolts are diffused by clouds into bursting balls of light — sometimes looking, as Sally Ride wrote, like a transcontinental brigade tossing fireworks from cloud to cloud. This view over the South China Sea near Borneo, photographed Oct 28, 2026, shows lightning illuminating thunderstorm tops, the lights of Singapore at left, and blue fishing-boat lights scattered across the dark sea. NASA estimates about 2,000 thunderstorms are active on Earth at any moment, producing nearly 60 lightning flashes per second.
